extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and practicing stand-up comedians and comedy writers
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, stage-focused guidance on writing jokes, developing a comedic voice, performing stand-up, sequencing a set, and navigating the comedy industry and writing for other media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovering Your Comedy Voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Finding what makes you funny; identifying what sets you apart and the core of your comedic identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises: deep self-reflection, list pet peeves, cultural observations, and personal stories to uncover recurring themes and patterns; examine whether you lean toward observational comedy, storytelling, political satire, etc.; connect individuality with audience through relatable expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding Comedy Genres and Styles
rubrics_metrics.description: Know different genres (e.g., slapstick, dark comedy, improvisational) and their conventions, audience expectations, and stylistic nuances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study genres to see where your predilections fit and incorporate elements from other styles to enrich your act; understanding conventions helps tailor material appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know Your Audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Tailor material to the tastes and sensibilities of the audience because what’s funny to one group may not land with another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt jokes, tone, and references to the audience; reading demographic and situational cues helps ensure humor resonates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setup, Punchline, and Tags (Joke Structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: The basic building blocks of a joke: the setup introduces the premise, the punchline subverts expectation, and tags are extra punchlines that follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Setup should be clear, concise, and relatable without revealing too much; punchlines rely on surprise and brevity; tags extend laughs on the same topic to maximize comedic potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing and Refining Jokes
rubrics_metrics.description: From observation to drafting setups and punchlines, then iterating to sharpen language, timing, and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect material from everyday experiences and absurdities; test jokes in different environments, cut unnecessary words, sharpen punchlines, adjust timing; iterative process informed by audience reactions is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-Laughs Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If a joke doesn’t get at least three laughs in its telling (often via tags), it should be reworked or discarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a quality filter to maintain strong material throughout a set; aim for multiple laughs from a single premise where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Predictability
rubrics_metrics.description: Jokes that follow too-familiar patterns or lack a surprising twist fail to engage the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive to flip everyday situations on their head and think outside expected patterns to preserve surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Over-Explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t overload the setup with unnecessary detail; over-explanation dilutes the punchline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brevity is critical—refine setups to their essential elements so the punchline remains sharp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Offensive or Alienating Humor (Be Mindful of Shock Value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relying on shock or alienation can limit appeal and has social consequences; prefer wit over pure shock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the audience and broader societal context; wit and sophistication broaden appeal and demonstrate comedic skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage Presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanding attention and engaging the audience through confident openings, eye contact, body language, and energetic projection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a strong opening to set the tone; practice expressive body language and natural connection techniques to make audiences feel engaged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing Stage Fright
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical techniques to overcome anxiety and nervousness before performing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use deep breathing, visualization, physical warm-ups, and thorough preparation (know your material) to reduce nerves; connecting with audience vulnerability can also help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing, Rhythm, and Physicality
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing is the backbone of comedy; rhythm and physical performance affect joke delivery and reception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know when to pause and when to deliver punchlines; practice with a metronome, record performances, rehearse to gauge natural speech rhythms; use physicality deliberately to enhance jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong Opening
rubrics_metrics.description: Start with a sharp, relatable, and proven joke to capture attention and signal who you are.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use material that has worked in multiple settings; a strong opening breaks the ice and establishes expectations for the set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitions Between Jokes
rubrics_metrics.description: Seamless transitions maintain flow and prevent a set from feeling disjointed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link jokes thematically or narratively; group related jokes (e.g., about relationships) and find natural connections to keep the audience following the logical thread.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Varying tempo and grouping different-length pieces to keep audience engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mix short punchy jokes with longer story-driven bits; adjust tempo based on audience reactions to maximize laughter and avoid fatigue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptability / Reading the Room
rubrics_metrics.description: Be prepared to modify delivery, shuffle or drop jokes, and extend segments based on live audience response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flexibility helps you stay in control of momentum; drop material that’s falling flat and exploit bits that get strong reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong Closing
rubrics_metrics.description: End with one of your strongest pieces to leave a lasting, positive impression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Close on a guaranteed big laugh so audiences leave on a high note and remember your set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearse the Entire Set
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice the full performance, not just isolated jokes, to internalize flow and timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rehearsal helps fine-tune transitions and pacing and makes the set feel natural and polished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Networking
rubrics_metrics.description: Build meaningful relationships with comedians, agents, bookers, and producers to open opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend open mics and industry events, be a positive presence, support others’ performances, offer help—genuine connections matter more than transactional interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand Industry Expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Know the needs and conventions of clubs, festivals, TV networks, and streaming platforms to target efforts effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research where you fit in the comedy landscape and learn what different venues and platforms expect in style, length, and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing and Online Presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Use platforms like YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok to showcase work and attract bookers and agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a professionally managed online presence; prepare a demo reel, resume, and headshots for auditions and representation inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audition Preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare for auditions by researching the show/event, understanding its style and audience, and tailoring your performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidence and professionalism during auditions leave lasting impressions; tailor material and presentation to the opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Securing Representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Find agents or managers with industry contacts and experience to help land opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research potential reps, present a compelling case about your unique voice and potential, and demonstrate professionalism and readiness as a client.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing for Television: Character- and Situation-Driven Humor
rubrics_metrics.description: TV comedy depends on character development and situational contexts rather than standalone stand-up jokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand the show's format and audience; craft dialogue that advances plot while integrating humor; adapt to episodic pacing and character consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration in TV Writers' Rooms
rubrics_metrics.description: TV writing is collaborative—ideas are pitched, refined, and rewritten collectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn to build on others' ideas, accept feedback, and contribute constructively to the writers' room process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing for Film: Three-Act Structure and Sustaining Humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Screenplays require longer-form plotting (three-act structure), sustained character arcs, and humor woven through a longer narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pace humor across acts, develop well-rounded characters and plot, and emphasize visual and physical comedy suitable for the medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous Learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain longevity by continually learning—workshops, seminars, self-study, and analyzing other comedians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stay informed about trends and audience preferences; refresh material with current events and cultural shifts to remain relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with Rejection and Setbacks
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop resilience; view rejection as learning opportunities rather than failures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek feedback from peers, mentors, and audiences; accept criticism constructively and use it to iterate and improve material and performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Branding
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a distinct, recognizable comedic persona and consistently project it across platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hone a unique voice and ensure it’s reflected in live performances, social media, and professional materials to build a dedicated fan base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain Professional Reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Professionalism, reliability, and a good attitude are critical because the comedy industry is close-knit and reputation spreads quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be dependable and courteous to open doors; unprofessional behavior can quickly close opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversification of Skills and Income Streams
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore other avenues—TV writing, acting, producing—to sustain career and income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversifying keeps creative muscles engaged and provides additional opportunities beyond stand-up gigs.
